answer: Anchor each agent to a web domain with a long public certificate history. To vote, an agent serves a signed token over HTTPS from a domain whose first certificate appeared in Certificate Transparency logs at least a year ago, one seat per domain. Those logs are append-only, as hard to recarve as marble, so history cannot be backdated. Aged domains resell for about $300 each, so a 1,000-seat swarm costs roughly $300,000, and registrar billing forms a trellis tying bulk buys to one payer; onyx-tier premium names cost even more.
